items.title: No local explanation of why patients return
items.whyItMatters: The expansion decision needs to know whether returns are avoidable and what would prevent them.
items.opportunity: Ask patients who returned, their carers and the clinicians involved how the return came about.

items.title: The dashboard comparison ignores case mix
items.whyItMatters: A matched cohort found no clear difference after adjustment (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Do not treat the 17 against 12 percent gap as an effect; describe case mix alongside the interviews.

items.title: Carers' night-time burden is unmeasured
items.whyItMatters: Carers with health problems or other duties carry the most strain, and carer breakdown precedes many readmissions (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Include carers as a separate participant group with their own interview guide.

items.title: Patients with limited English or no carer are hard to reach
items.whyItMatters: Patients living alone were readmitted more often in the retrieved matched cohort and are the least likely to volunteer.
items.opportunity: Sample deliberately for patients living alone and offer interpreters.

errorsFound: The request treats the dashboard gap as established; the retrieved matched cohort suggests case mix may explain part of it.
reevaluation: The gaps point to an explanatory qualitative study of recent readmissions rather than a larger comparison of rates.
summary: Four gaps; the missing local explanation and carer burden are high severity.
